text: The gap that counts as an outlier, its unit and the rule that settles it are taken as one versioned reference-data row of rwb-case (default ruling of Template and Rules v1 §R3: parameters and reference data belong to P3 rwb-case) or as a row of the S1 rule package read through rwb-decision, with their valid-from date and their version; the step reads whichever is in force on the business date and flags nothing, recording the rule gap, where neither can be resolved. No percentage, distance, limit or appraisal type is written in code, as a default or as a branch of the build.
why: The FSD requires the comparison and BR-S1-003 forbids a business value in code, but no source in the set gives the limit, its unit or the rule id, and the S1 rule package is Phase 2. A default ruling already exists for parameters and reference data, so the read is assumed rather than invented; the value itself stays open as CG-B2-S1-003-1 and the business owner confirms it before the wave 3 entry gate.

text: The market value of the asset is consumed as a declared input element of the outlier step, carrying the market value, its source name, its source date and its version, and this service asserts no model call of its own. Until one owner publishes it, the element is carried on the rwb-source-data data product read together with the appraisal; if the agent runtime is chosen instead, the same element arrives on the rwb-agent contract and the story gains a class C dependency of DP-20 at that point and not before.
why: The FSD and the feature sheet name a model gateway with no owner, operation, path or element, and the pattern set of this legacy key does not carry DP-20, so a direct agent dependency would add a dependency the plan does not hold. The benchmark is still needed for the comparison, so the least invasive reading is to treat it as an input fact and to record the owner as not published (CG-B2-S1-003-2).

text: The previous value is the latest prior appraisal of the same asset_key on the rwb-source-data data product, taken by appraisal date, and the basis used and its date are recorded on every check. If the business owner prefers the last accepted value of valuation_ext, the change is one read and the recorded basis, and the shape of the answer and the record does not change.
why: The legacy criterion and the FSD compare the new value with 'the previous value' and no source defines it, while FEAT-VAL-02 links every appraisal to the asset by business key and FEAT-VAL-04 accepts a value. The prior appraisal of the same asset is the only basis the published elements support without a new field, so it is assumed and the flag carries the basis for audit (CG-B2-S1-003-3).

text: The outlier flag, its reasons and the two gaps are held in the local decision record of DP-03 for wave 3, and the service declares no table and no column of its own until the data owner of the service names the store. If `valuation` in rwb_valuation or `valuation_ext` is confirmed as the store, the DB story of the service adds the columns in its own Flyway sequence and the contract baseline declares the elements in a minor version.
why: The Ownership Map gives S1 no table, TSD S1 T3.1 declares `valuation` as a NEW table and the FSD holds the acceptance in `recovery.valuation_ext`, so three readings are open and none places the flag (CG-B2-S1-003-4). Holding the flag in the decision record keeps the proof of the check without pre-empting the schema decision, and it breaks no rule because the record is the object that must exist before the flag is presented.

text: The six consumed rows of the outlier step are declared with their owner, their use, one hop and a 2 s budget, and each row whose operation name is not published carries the placeholder and its gap instead of a path: the rwb-source-data data product, the market benchmark, the rwb-case reference data of the gap rule, the rwb-case case state, the rwb-decision rule-in-force and decision-log read, and the rwb-access authorise call. The build runs against the documented fakes of the contract baseline on Day 1, and the absent contract dependencies of this slice are recorded rather than treated as none.
why: The plan gives the slice an empty contract-dependency list while the FSD, the TSD and the screen states require five owners' facts, and only the case read and the authorise call have a published shape (CG-B2-S1-003-5). Root AGENTS.md rule 8 forbids inventing a path, so the rows carry the placeholder and the build is decoupled by the fakes, which is the rule R5.7 already sets for class C.

text: The outlier check is started as the value step of RouteDecisionWorkflow when the route assessment reaches it, and again on the re-assessment that follows a new appraisal or a corrected value; the service declares no event subscription, no Schedule and no job, because the ownership rows give S1 none. A valuer-report event or a batch-completion trigger, if it is wanted later, is a new event of the owner that publishes it and a new story of this service.
why: The FSD names three possible triggers in one phrase without choosing one, R-DIS-16 has the check follow the valuer report and R-UNI-37 re-runs the gates after a correction, while the ownership rows give the service no event and no job (CG-B2-S1-003-6). Running the step from the workflow the map already gives the service is the only reading that needs no new ownership row and no unnamed subscription.

text: The outlier element of the route answer is declared by the contract baseline as one additive optional element of `Approval` under the draft name `appraisalOutlier`, carrying the market gap, the previous-value gap, the flag, its reasons, the threshold version and the rule version, and it is marked as not published with its gap. Every published element keeps its name, its type and its nullability, and the API owner may rename the draft element at the tag without a major version while no consumer of it is released.
why: The only operation of this key publishes an `Approval` with no appraisal, market or flag element, and no schema, example or component names one, so the element is a realignment addition rather than a published shape (CG-B2-S1-003-7). Naming it as a draft and marking it keeps the document usable on Day 1 without a path or a field being invented as if it were published, and the additive rule of BR3 keeps the change compatible.
